# **PA Setup**

## ***Components***

* Powered speaker(s)  
* Mixer  
* Cables  
* Microphone(s)  
* Musical instrument(s)

## ***Setup***

1. Plug in speaker(s) and mixer to AC power outlet using a “kettle lead” or “IEC cord”. **Do not turn on yet\!**  
2. Connect mixer to speakers using 3-pin XLR cables. “Main” output on mixer to input 1 on speaker(s). Make sure speaker input is switched to “line”, not “microphone”.  
3. Connect microphone to mixer channel 1 using an XLR cable  
4. Connect musical instrument(s) using a DI (Direct Input) box.   
   1. Use a ¼” phone plug cable to connect the instrument to the DI   
   2. Use an XLR cable to connect the DI box to a microphone input on the mixer  
5. Normalize controls on mixer and speaker  
   1. Pull all the faders all the way down  
   2. EQ controls to center (straight up)  
   3. Aux controls all the way counter-clockwise  
   4. Speaker level at 0 (in the middle or straight up)  
6. Turn on mixer power  
7. Turn on speaker power  
8. Adjusts input gain(s) (small knob at top of each microphone channel strip on the mixer)  
   1. Have somebody produce a signal in into the mic  
   2. Turn up the gain until the red light flashes, then reduce the gain until it stops  
   3. Repeat for other mics and instruments  
9. Turn up master faders to the sweet spot between \-3dB and 0dB  
10. Turn up channel fader(s) to desired level

## ***General rules of thumb***

* Always use XLR cables for line-level signals when possible (mixer to speakers). You can use ¼” phone plug cables in a pinch, but this can introduce unwanted noise  
* Always turn on the mixer before you turn on the speaker(s), and turn off the speaker(s) before you turn off the mixer  
* Always turn levels down before powering up or down  
* keep microphones behind speakers, and never point a microphone at speakers reduce feedback)  
* Use EQ sparingly or not at all. It’s usually better to cut frequencies than boost.
